# Alive with Their Lord - the Prophet and the Imams after Death in the Hadith Corpus

No verse of the Qur'an tells a believer to ask a deceased Imam for help, and the nearest texts, among them the instruction to come to the Messenger while he is alive and seek Allah's forgiveness with his prayer for them (Qur'an 4:64), concern the living. The question is whether the book and the reports together support the practice, and what exactly they support when they do. The Imams below are the twelve descendants of the Prophet through Ali and Fatima, and the corpus is the hadith literature of the school beside the Sunni books the later sections quote. Three passages supply principles. The martyrs are alive with their Lord, receiving provision (Qur'an 3:169). Allah, His Messenger and the believers see the deeds that people do (Qur'an 9:105). A servant can be granted an extraordinary capacity, and using it remains Allah's favour (Qur'an 27:40). None of these verses names a grave, a visitor, or a request.

The reports supply that step. A person with a need is told to stand at the head of al-Husayn ﵇ and address him with the words, I testify that you witness my standing and hear my words, and that you are alive with your Lord receiving provision, so ask your Lord and my Lord to fulfil my needs. Other reports describe the dead Imam seeing his visitors by name and praying for the one who weeps at his grave, the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams receiving further knowledge after death, and in several accounts the dead appearing to the living while awake.

Each report below is quoted as a contiguous extract from its source, with the chain where the source prints one.

| Evidence | What it carries | Chain as printed |
|---|---|---|
| [The grave instruction](#the-instruction-at-the-grave) | Address al-Husayn ﵇, you hear me, you are alive, ask Allah for me | Ibn Fahd introduces it with "it is reported from al-Sadiq ﵇", without an isnad (chain) |
| [A chained instruction for both graves](#the-instruction-at-the-grave) | Visit Ali ﵇ and al-Husayn ﵇ and turn there with your needs | Ibn Uqda, through Hammad ibn Yala, from Hassan ibn Mihran |
| [The visitation texts](#the-instruction-at-the-grave) | The visitor addresses al-Husayn ﵇ and seeks Allah through him | Liturgies in Kamil al-Ziyarat and Tahdhib al-Ahkam |
| [Al-Husayn ﵇ sees his visitors](#the-dead-who-see-and-act) | He knows them by name, seeks forgiveness for the one who weeps, and asks his father to seek it | Two routes in Kamil al-Ziyarat, both through al-Asamm |
| [Knowledge after death](#knowledge-that-keeps-arriving) | The souls of dead prophets and trustees ascend and return with new knowledge | al-Kafi, several routes, and Basa'ir al-Darajat |
| [The bodies](#their-bodies-raised-or-preserved) | Raised after three days, or forty days, or preserved; the corpus carries all three | al-Kafi 4:567, Tahdhib 6:106-107, al-Amali, surveyed in Mukhtasar Mufid |
| [Appearances awake and in dreams](#seen-awake-and-in-dreams) | The Prophet ﷺ shown to Abu Bakr; dreams distinguished from waking encounters | al-Kafi 1:580-581 through Ibn al-Jarish; Basa'ir; al-Amali |
| [The Sunni canon](#the-same-act-in-the-sunni-canon) | The Prophet's ﷺ own supplication (du'a) with its turn through him; al-Hakim's text adds the vocative, and a Companion teaches it after his death | Tirmidhi hasan sahih gharib; al-Hakim sahih al-isnad; the story in al-Zabidi's takhrij (documentation) |
| [The hearing objection](#the-hearing-objection) | That the dead do not hear, from Qur'an 27:80 and 35:22 | Stated by Ibn Taymiyya, Majmu al-Fatawa 1:171; answered by al-Shinqiti's two readings and Abu Dawud's report |

## What the Qur'an Establishes

The reports themselves quote this verse.

> [!quote]- Qur'an 3:169
> وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمْوَٰتًۢا ۚ بَلْ أَحْيَآءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ
>
> *wa-la tahsabanna alladhina qutilu fi sabili Allahi amwatan, bal ahyaanun 'inda rabbihim yurzaqun*
>
> Do not suppose that those who have been killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.

It does not state that every martyr hears every caller, and it does not describe the condition or the location of the buried body. The reports examined below apply exactly this verse's language to al-Husayn ﵇ and then add hearing, recognition, and prayer.

> [!quote]- Qur'an 9:105
> وَقُلِ ٱعْمَلُوا۟ فَسَيَرَى ٱللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۖ وَسَتُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ عَٰلِمِ ٱلْغَيْبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
>
> *wa-qul i'malu fa-sayara Allahu 'amalakum wa-rasuluhu wa-l-mu'minun*
>
> Say, "Act. God will see your deeds, as will His Messenger and the believers. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do."

Who "the believers" are, and what this seeing means after the Prophet's ﷺ death, is what the reports interpret.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 267
> (باب) * (عرض الأعمال على النبي ﵌ والأئمة ﵈) * 1 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن الحسين بن سعيد ، عن القاسم بن محمد ، عن علي بن أبي حمزة ، عن أبي بصير ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : تعرض الأعمال على رسول الله ﵌ أعمال العباد (1) كل صباح أبرارها وفجارها فاحذروها ، وهو قول الله تعالى : " اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله (4) " وسكت .
>
> Chapter on the presentation of deeds to the Prophet and the Imams.
>
> 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, "The deeds of servants, both their righteous deeds and their wicked deeds, are presented to the Messenger of God every morning. So beware of them. This is the saying of God Most High, 'Act, and God will see your deed, and His Messenger.'" Then he fell silent.

The report has deeds presented to the Messenger ﷺ every morning, the righteous and the sinful among them, and reads this as the meaning of Qur'an 9:105. The chains cite the Imams by their honorific names, Abu Abd Allah for al-Sadiq, Abu Ja'far for al-Baqir, and Abu Ja'far the Second, in one chain below, for al-Jawad. A second report on the same page describes his grief at the disobedience he sees among the deeds, and the grave instruction below addresses al-Husayn by his own kunya, Abu Abd Allah, the same name al-Sadiq carries in the chains.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 267
> 3 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن عثمان بن عيسى ، عن سماعة ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : سمعته يقول : مالكم تسوؤن رسول الله ﵌ ؟ ! فقال رجل : كيف نسوؤه ؟ فقال : أما تعلمون أن أعمالكم تعرض عليه ، فإذا رأى فيها معصية ساءه ذلك ، فلا تسوؤا رسول الله وسروه .
>
> 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, "I heard him say, 'Why do you offend the Messenger of God?'
>
> A man said, 'How do we offend him?'
>
> He said, 'Do you not know that your deeds are presented to him? When he sees disobedience among them, that grieves him. So do not offend the Messenger of God. Make him glad.'"

Al-Saffar's Basa'ir al-Darajat gathers the same doctrine under a chapter heading that names the dead Imams explicitly.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , al-Saffar, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 447
> (5) باب عرض الأعمال على الأئمة الاحياء والأموات (1) حدثنا محمد بن الحسين ويعقوب بن يزيد عن ابن أبي عمير عن ابن أذينة عن بريد العجلي قال كنت عند أبي عبد الله ع فسألته عن قوله تعالى اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون قال إيانا عنى .
>
> 5. Chapter on the presentation of deeds to the Imams, living and dead (1).
>
> Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Yaqub ibn Yazid related to us, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Burayd al-Ijli, who said, "I was with Abu Abd Allah and asked him about the saying of God Most High, 'Act, and God will see your deed, and His Messenger and the believers.' He said, 'He meant us.'"

A second report of the al-Kafi chapter identifies "the believers" of the verse as the Imams.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 267
> 2 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن الحسين بن سعيد ، عن النضر بن سويد ، عن يحيى الحلبي ، عن عبد الحميد الطائي ، عن يعقوب بن شعيب قال : سألت أبا عبد الله ﵇ عن قول الله ﷿ : " اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون " قال : هم الأئمة .
>
> 2. A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Abd al-Hamid al-Tai, from Yaqub ibn Shuayb, who said, "I asked Abu Abd Allah about the saying of God, 'Act, and God will see your deed, and His Messenger and the believers.' He said, 'They are the Imams.'"

A companion asks Imam al-Rida ﵇ to pray for him and his household and the report has the Imam answer with the doctrine and its verse reading.

> [!info]- Imam al-Rida , al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 267
> 4 - علي ، عن أبيه ، عن القاسم بن محمد ، عن الزيات ، عن عبد الله بن أبان الزيات وكان مكينا عند الرضا ﵇ قال : قلت للرضا ﵇ : ادع الله لي ولأهل بيتي فقال : أو لست أفعل ؟ والله إن أعمالكم لتعرض علي في كل يوم وليلة ، قال : فاستعظمت
>
> 4. Ali, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Zayyat, from Abd Allah ibn Aban al-Zayyat, who was held in high standing by al-Rida, who said, "I said to al-Rida, 'Pray to God for me and for my household.' He said, 'Do I not do so? By God, your deeds are presented to me every day and night.'" He said, "I considered

> [!info]- Imam al-Rida , al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 268 (continued)
> ذلك ، فقال لي : أما تقرء كتاب الله ﷿ : " وقل اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون " ؟ قال : هو والله علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ (1) .
>
> that a grave matter." He said to me, "Have you not read the Book of God, 'Say, Act, and God will see your deed, and His Messenger and the believers'?" He said, "By God, it is Ali ibn Abi Talib (1)."

Taken together, the verse and these reports support continued awareness of what the living do. Awareness of deeds is not yet hearing of every spoken appeal; that further step comes from the grave reports, not from this verse.

The third passage answers a narrower objection, from the story of Sulayman and the Queen of Saba's throne.

> [!quote]- Qur'an 27:40
> قَالَ ٱلَّذِى عِندَهُۥ عِلْمٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِندَهُۥ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضْلِ رَبِّى لِيَبْلُوَنِىٓ ءَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ ۖ وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّى غَنِىٌّۭ كَرِيمٌۭ
>
> *qala alladhi 'indahu 'ilmun min al-kitabi ana atika bihi qabla an yartadda ilayka tarfuk, falamma ra'ahu mustaqirran 'indahu qala hadha min fadli rabbi*
>
> The one who had knowledge from the Book said, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." Then, when he saw it settled before him, he said, "This is from the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will give thanks or be ungrateful. Whoever gives thanks gives thanks only for his own sake. Whoever is ungrateful, then my Lord is Self-Sufficient and Generous."

The passage establishes that Allah can grant a servant an extraordinary capacity and that its use remains Allah's favour, not the servant's independent power. The man in the verse was alive. The verse does not establish action after death; it removes the assumption that no servant of Allah could ever be granted such a capacity at all.

## The Instruction at the Grave

The most direct text is an instruction for a person with a need. Ibn Fahd al-Hilli records it in the fifth category of supplications, the category combined with a place.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , attributed by Ibn Fahd al-Hilli, Uddat al-Da'i, p. 56
> القسم الخامس ما يتركب من الدعا والمكان (2) مثل ما روى عن الصادق (ع) من كان له حاجة إلى الله ﷿ فليقف عند رأس الحسين ﵇ وليقل : (يا أبا عبد الله اشهد انك تشهد مقامي وتسمع كلامي وانك حي عند ربك ترزق فاسئل ربك وربى في قضاء حوائجي) فإنها تقضى انشاء الله تعالى .
>
> The fifth section, on what is composed of supplication and place (2). An example is what was narrated from al-Sadiq. Whoever has a need from God, let him stand at the head of al-Husayn and say, "O Abu Abd Allah, I bear witness that you witness my standing place and hear my words, and that you are alive and provided for by your Lord. So ask your Lord and my Lord concerning the fulfillment of my needs." They will be fulfilled, if God Most High wills.

The formula joins the three claims the question needs, witness, life in the words of Qur'an 3:169, and the request. The grant is sought from Allah; the Imam is asked to pray, not to grant. The limit is the chain. Ibn Fahd introduces the report with "it is reported from al-Sadiq ﵇" and prints no chain of transmission, isnad, at this locus, so the instruction cannot be presented as established, graded sahih, on this citation alone.

Al-Nuri al-Tabrisi relays the same text with its setting.

> [!info]- The same instruction relayed in al-Nuri al-Tabrisi, Mustadrak al-Wasa'il, vol. 10, p. 345
> 59 - (باب استحباب الاكثار من الدعاء وطلب الحوائج عند قبر الحسين (﵇)) (12149) 1 - أحمد بن فهد في عده الداعي : روي عن الصادق (﵇) : . من كانت له حاجة إلى الله عز ووجل ، فليقف عند رأس الحسين (﵇) وليقل : يا با عبد الله أشهد أنك تشهد مقامي وتسمع كلامي ، وأنك حي عند ربك ترزق ، فاسأل ربك وربي في قضاء حوائجي ، فإنها تقضى إن شاء الله تعالى .
>
> 59. Chapter on the recommendation to make many supplications and seek one's needs at the grave of al-Husayn.
>
> (12149) 1. Ahmad ibn Fahd, in Uddat al-Dai, narrated from al-Sadiq. Whoever has a need from God, Mighty and Majestic, let him stand at the head of al-Husayn and say, "O Abu Abd Allah, I bear witness that you witness my standing place and hear my words, and that you are alive and provided for by your Lord. So ask your Lord and my Lord concerning the fulfillment of my needs." They will be fulfilled, if God Most High wills.

The relay confirms the attribution as Ibn Fahd's book transmits it and shows the later tradition reading it as an instruction to seek needs at the grave. It adds no independent chain.

The following page of Uddat al-Da'i carries a related report in which an Imam speaks of his own future grave. A man cheated of his stipend asked Imam al-Hadi ﵇ to intercede, and the report has the Imam teach him a supplication instead. The extract prints only the closing words, al-Fath is a courtier of the story's caliph, and the supplication is the one the story has just taught.

> [!info]- Imam al-Hadi , in Ibn Fahd al-Hilli, Uddat al-Da'i, p. 57
> قال ( ع ) : ان الفتح يوالينا بظاهره دون باطنه ، الدعا لمن دعا به بشرط ان يوالينا أهل البيت ، لكن هذا الدعا كثير اما ا دعو به عند الحوائج فتقضى ، وقد سئلت الله ﷿ ان لا يدعو به بعدى أحد عند قبري الا استجيب له
>
> He said, "Al-Fath is allied with us outwardly but not inwardly. This supplication is for whoever supplicates with it, on condition that he be loyal to us, the People of the House. Yet this supplication is abundant. Whenever I supplicate with it in times of need, the needs are fulfilled. I have asked Allah that no one after me should supplicate with it at my grave without being answered."

The Imam's own words as reported assume a supplication used at a grave after death and an answer from Allah; the inference rests on the wording, not on the chain's grade.

A report with a stated chain names both graves.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq  to Hassan ibn Mihran, in Ibn Uqda, Fada'il Amir al-Mu'minin, p. 139
> 134 - ابن عقدة ، قال : حدّثنا حمّاد بن يعلى ، قال : أخبرني حسّان بن مهران الجمّال ، قال : قال لي جعفر بن محمّد : يا حسّان أتزور قبور الشهداء قبلكم ؟ قلت : أيّ الشهداء ؟ قال : عليّ وحسين . قلت : إنّا نزورهما فنكثر . قال : أولئك الشهداء المرزوقين ، فزوروهم وافزعوا عندهم بحوائجكم ، فلو يكونون منّا كموضعهم منكم لاتّخذناهم هجرة (2) .
>
> 134. Ibn Uqda said, Hammad ibn Yala related to us. Hassan ibn Mihran al-Jammal told me that Jafar ibn Muhammad said to me, "O Hassan, do you visit the graves of the martyrs before you?"
>
> I said, "Which martyrs?"
>
> He said, "Ali and Husayn."
>
> I said, "We visit them often."
>
> He said, "Those are martyrs who are provided for. Visit them and turn there with your needs. If they were among us as they are among you, we would have made them a place of migration (2)."

Ali ﵇, the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law, and al-Husayn ﵇, his grandson, are named after their deaths, called the martyrs who receive provision, the language of Qur'an 3:169 again, and the instruction is to visit them and turn there with one's needs. Ibn Tawus transmits the report with the same named route in Farhat al-Ghari (pp. 106-107), relaying it through Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, who is Ibn Uqda. The Imam's us and you place the two graves in the visitor's Iraq against his own Arabia. "Turn there with your needs" does not by itself specify whether one asks them to intercede or asks Allah at their graves. The Uddat al-Da'i formula supplies that specification, and it is the weaker attested of the two texts.

The visitation liturgies put the same request in the visitor's mouth in plainer words.

> [!note]- The visitation text, in Ibn Qulawayh, Kamil al-Ziyarat, p. 419
> يا أبا عبد الله يا حسين ابن رسول الله ، جئتك مستشفعا بك إلى الله ، اللهم إني أستشفع إليك بولد حبيبك ، وبالملائكة الذين يضجون عليه ويبكون ويصرخون ، لا يفترون ولا يسأمون ، وهم من خشيتك مشفقون ، ومن عذابك حذرون . لا تغيرهم الأيام ولا يهرمون ، في نواحي الحير يشهقون ، وسيدهم يرى ما يصنعون وما فيه يتقلبون ، قد انهملت (2) منهم العيون فلا ترقأ (3) ، واشتد منهم الحزن بحرقة لا تطفأ .
>
> O Abu Abd Allah, O Husayn, son of the Messenger of God, I have come to you seeking your intercession with God. O God, I seek intercession from You through the child of Your Beloved, and through the angels who cry aloud over him, weep, and call out. They neither slacken nor grow weary. They are apprehensive out of fear of You and wary of Your punishment.
>
> The days do not change them, nor do they grow old. In the precincts of al-Ha'ir they sob, and their master sees what they do and the state in which they turn. Tears have poured from their eyes and do not cease, and their grief has become intense with a burning that is not extinguished.

Al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam carries the ziyarah taught for the grave with the same structure.

> [!note]- The ziyarah taught for the grave, in al-Tusi, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, p. 60
> اللهم أبلغ روحه وجسده في ساعتي هذه وفي كل ساعة تحية مني كثيرة وسلاما ، آمنا بالله وحده واتبعنا الرسول فاكتبنا مع الشاهدين ، السلام عليك يا ابن رسول الله اتيتك بأبي أنت وأمي زائرا وافدا إليك متوجها بك إلى الله ربك وربي لينجح بك حوائجي ويعطيني بك سؤلي فاشفع لي عند ربك وكن لي شفيعا ، وقد جئتك هاربا من ذنوبي متنصلا إلى ربي من سئ عملي راجيا في موقفي هذا الخلاص من عقوبة ربي طامعا ان يستنقذني ربي بك من الردى ، اتيتك يا مولاي وافدا إليك إذ رغب عن زيارتك أهل الدنيا واليك كانت رحلتي ولك عبرتي وصرختي وعليك أسفي ولك نحيبي وزفرتي وعليك تحيتي وسلامي ، ألقيت رحلي بفنائك مستجيرا بك وبقبرك مما أخاف من عظيم جرمي واتيتك زائرا التمس ثبات القدم في الهجرة إليك ، وقد تيقنت ان الله ﷻ بكم ينفس الهم ، وبكم يكشف الكرب ، وبكم يباعدنا عن نائبات الزمان الكلب ، وبكم يفتح الله ، وبكم ينزل الغيث ، وبكم ينزل الرحمة ، وبكم يمسك الأرض ان تسيخ باهلها ، وبكم يثبت الله جبالها على مراسيها ، وقد توجهت إلى ربي يا سيدي في قضاء حوائجي ومغفرة ذنوبي فلا أخيبن من زوارك فقد خشيت ذلك أن لم تشفع لي ولا ينصرفن زوارك يا مولاي بالعطاء والحباء والخير والجزاء والمغفرة والرضا ، وانصرف انا مجبوها بذنوبي مردودا علي عملي فقد خيبت لما سلف مني ،
>
> O God, convey to his spirit and body, at this hour of mine and at every hour, abundant greetings and peace from me. We have believed in God alone and followed the Messenger, so write us among the witnesses. Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of God. May my father and mother be your ransom. I have come to you as a visitor and arrival, turning through you to God, your Lord and my Lord, so that through you my needs may be fulfilled and He may grant me my request through you. Intercede for me with your Lord and be an intercessor for me.
>
> I have come to you fleeing from my sins, renouncing my evil deeds before my Lord, hoping at this place where I stand for deliverance from the punishment of my Lord, and desiring that my Lord may rescue me through you from destruction. I have come to you, my master, arriving before you, when the people of this world have turned away from visiting you. My journey is to you, my tears and cry are for you, my sorrow is over you, and my wailing and sighing are for you. Upon you be my greeting and peace.
>
> I have set down my baggage in your courtyard, seeking your protection and that of your grave from what I fear because of the enormity of my crime. I have come to you as a visitor, seeking firmness of foot in migrating to you. I have become certain that through you God relieves distress, through you He removes affliction, through you He keeps us far from the calamities of harsh time, through you God opens the way, through you He sends down rain, through you He sends down mercy, through you He holds the earth back from sinking with its inhabitants, and through you God secures its mountains upon their anchors.
>
> I have turned to my Lord through you, my master, concerning the fulfillment of my needs and the forgiveness of my sins. Let me not be disappointed among your visitors, for I have feared that if you do not intercede for me, your visitors will depart, my master, with gifts, favors, goodness, recompense, forgiveness, and approval, while I return rebuffed because of my sins and my deeds are returned to me. I have indeed been disappointed because of what has preceded from me.

In these liturgies the Imam is addressed, heard in the sense the reports describe, and asked to intercede, and the visitor also seeks refuge in him and at his grave. Every effect the liturgies request is sought from Allah, and no text quoted gives the Imam an independent grant.

## The Dead Who See and Act

The longest report describing al-Husayn ﵇ after his death comes from a question about his grave.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq  to Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, in Ibn Qulawayh, Kamil al-Ziyarat, p. 206
> حدثني أبي ﵀ ، عن الحسين بن الحسن بن ابان ، عن الحسين بن سعيد ، عن عبد الله بن المغيرة ، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمان الأصم ، عن عبد الله بن بكير الأرجاني . وحدثني أبي ﵀ ، عن سعد بن عبد الله ، عن محمد بن الحسين ، عن محمد بن عبد الله بن زرارة ، عن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمان الأصم ، عن عبد الله بن بكير ، قال : حججت مع أبي عبد الله (﵇) - في حديث طويل - فقلت : يا بن رسول الله لو نبش قبر الحسين بن علي (﵉) هل كان يصاب في قبره شي ، فقال : يا بن بكير ما أعظم مسائلك ، ان الحسين (﵇) مع أبيه وأمه وأخيه في منزل رسول الله (﵌) ومعه يرزقون ويحبرون ، وانه لعن يمين العرش متعلق به يقول : يا رب أنجز لي ما وعدتني ، وانه لينظر إلى زواره وانه أعرف بهم وبأسمائهم وأسماء ابائهم وما في رحالهم من أحدهم بولده ، وانه لينظر إلى من يبكيه فيستغفر له ويسأل أباه الاستغفار له ويقول : أيها الباكي لو علمت ما أعد الله لك لفرحت أكثر مما حزنت وانه ليستغفر له من كل ذنب وخطيئة (2) .
>
> My father related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr al-Arjani. My father also related to me from Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Zurara, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, who said, "I made the pilgrimage with Abu Abd Allah, in a lengthy report. I said, 'Son of the Messenger of God, if the grave of al-Husayn ibn Ali were excavated, would anything be found in his grave?'
>
> He said, 'O Ibn Bukayr, how grave your questions are. Al-Husayn is with his father, his mother, and his brother in the abode of the Messenger of God. With him they are provided for and made joyful. He is at the right of the Throne, clinging to it, saying, "My Lord, fulfill for me what You promised me." He looks upon those who visit him. He knows them, their names, the names of their fathers, and what is in their baggage better than any one of them knows his own child. He looks upon the one who weeps for him, asks forgiveness for him, asks his father to seek forgiveness for him, and says, "O you who weep, if you knew what God has prepared for you, you would rejoice more than you grieved." He seeks forgiveness for him for every sin and wrongdoing.'

Both stated routes pass through Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm before Ibn Bukayr, so the two chains are not independent confirmations of one another. The actions described are seeing, recognizing, and asking, and the forgiveness is sought from Allah.

Ibn Qulawayh transmits a longer version of the same scene.

> [!info]- The second version of the Ibn Bukayr report, Kamil al-Ziyarat, pp. 543-544
> قلت : جعلت فداك أخبرني عن الحسين (﵇) لو نبش كانوا يجدون في قبره شيئا ، قال : يا بن بكير ما أعظم مسائلك الحسين (﵇) مع أبيه وأمه وأخيه الحسن في منزل رسول الله (﵌) ، يحبون كما يحبي ويرزقون كما يرزق ، فلو نبش في أيامه لوجد (4) ، واما اليوم فهو حي عند ربه ينظر إلى معسكره ، وينظر إلى العرش متى يؤمر ان يحمله ، وانه لعلى يمين
>
> I said, "May I be made your ransom, tell me about al-Husayn. If his grave were opened, would they find anything in it?"
>
> He said, "O son of Bukayr, how grave your questions are. Al-Husayn is with his father, his mother, and his brother al-Hasan in the abode of the Messenger of God. They are granted gifts as he is granted them, and are provided for as he is provided for. If his grave had been opened in his days, he would have been found. But today he is alive with his Lord. He looks upon his camp, and he looks upon the Throne, awaiting when he will be commanded to bear it. He is clinging to the right side of the

> [!info]- The second version, continued, Kamil al-Ziyarat, p. 544
> العرش متعلق ، يقول : يا رب انجز لي ما وعدتني . وانه لينظر إلى زواره وهو اعرف بهم وبأسماء آبائهم وبدرجاتهم وبمنزلتهم عند الله من أحدكم بولده وما في رحله ، وانه ليرى من يبكيه فيستغفر له رحمة له ويسأل أباه الاستغفار له ، ويقول : لو تعلم أيها الباكي ما أعد لك لفرحت أكثر مما جزعت ، فيستغفر له كل من سمع بكائه من الملائكة في السماء وفي الحائر ، وينقلب وما عليه من ذنب (1) .
>
> Throne, saying, "My Lord, fulfill for me what You promised me."
>
> He looks upon his visitors, and he knows them, their fathers' names, their ranks, and their standing before God better than any one of you knows his own child and what is in his saddlebag. He sees whoever weeps for him, so he seeks forgiveness for him out of mercy for him, and asks his father to seek forgiveness for him. He says, "O weeper, if you knew what has been prepared for you, you would rejoice more than you grieve." Everyone who hears his weeping among the angels in heaven and in al-Ha'ir seeks forgiveness for him. He returns with no sin upon him.

The added phrase answers the question Ibn Bukayr asked about the grave's contents, if it had been opened in his days he would have been found, and as for today he is alive with his Lord, and it belongs with the body texts below. This version also ends with the weeper returning with no sin upon him.

The corpus reports the same awareness for ordinary dead believers, which removes the assumption that this is a doctrine invented only for Imams.

> [!info]- The dead believer and his visitor, al-Kafi, vol. 3, p. 232
> 4 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن عن إسحاق بن عمار ، عن أبي الحسن (﵇) قال : قلت له : المؤمن يعلم بمن يزور قبره ؟ قال : نعم ولا يزال مستأنسا به ما دام عند قبره فإذا قام وانصرف من قبره دخله من انصرافه عن قبره وحشة .
>
> 4. A number of our companions, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu al-Hasan, who said, "I said to him, 'Does a believer know who visits his grave?' He said, 'Yes. He remains comforted by him as long as he is at his grave. When he rises and departs from his grave, loneliness enters him because of his departure from his grave.'"

The same volume of al-Kafi carries a chapter titled "the dead person visits his family" (vol. 3, pp. 234-235). The believer visits his household in the form the reports describe, sees what pleases him, and some visit every Friday and some according to their deeds. Ali ﵇ instructs the living, in a route that again passes through al-Asamm.

> [!info]- Ali ibn Abi Talib , relayed by al-Sadiq , al-Kafi, vol. 3, p. 234
> وعن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن الأصم ، عن حريز ، عن محمد بن مسلم ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : قال أمير المؤمنين (﵇) زوروا موتاكم فإنهم يفرحون بزيارتكم وليطلب أحدكم حاجته عند قبر أبيه وعند قبر أمه بما يدعو لهما
>
> From Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abd Allah, who said that the Commander of the Faithful said, "Visit your dead, for they rejoice at your visiting them. Let each of you seek his need at the grave of his father and at the grave of his mother by praying for them."

The reports about the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams ﵈ stand within the corpus's wider body of reports, not as an exception to it.

A report in Basa'ir al-Darajat has the Imam state the principle in one line.

> [!info]- Samaa and the deceased Imam, in al-Saffar, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 295
> (4) حدثنا محمد بن عيسى عن محمد بن سنان عن عمار بن مروان عن سماعة قال دخلت على أبى عبد الله ﵇ وانا أحدث نفسي فرعاني فقال مالك تحدث نفسك تشتهى ان ترى أبا جعفر ﵇ قلت نعم قال قم فادخل البيت فإذا هو أبو جعفر ﵇ قال اتى قوم من الشيعة الحسن بن علي ﵇ بعد قتل أمير المؤمنين ﵇ فسألوه قال تعرفون أمير المؤمنين ﵇ إذا رأيتموه قالوا نعم قال فارفعوا الستر فرفعوه فإذا هم بأمير المؤمنين ﵇ لا ينكرونه وقال أمير المؤمنين ﵇ يموت من مات منا وليس بميت ويبقى من بقي منا حجة عليكم .
>
> 4. Muhammad ibn Isa related to us from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Sama'ah, who said, "I entered upon Abu Abd Allah while I was speaking to myself. He noticed me and said, 'What is the matter with you, speaking to yourself? Do you wish to see Abu Ja'far?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Rise and enter the house.' There was Abu Ja'far."
>
> He said, "A group of the Shi'a came to al-Hasan ibn Ali after the killing of the Commander of the Faithful and asked him, 'Will you recognize the Commander of the Faithful when you see him?' They said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Then raise the curtain.' They raised it, and there was the Commander of the Faithful, whom they did not fail to recognize. The Commander of the Faithful said, 'Whoever of us dies does not die, and whoever of us remains is a proof against you.'"

In the earlier scene it gives, al-Hasan ﵇ raised the curtain for a group of Shi'a after the killing of Ali ﵇, and the summary is Ali's own, whoever of us dies is not dead, and whoever remains of us is a proof against you. The chains also cite Abu al-Hasan, in the report on the dead believer's visits, for one of the later Imams; the chain does not print which. Seeing the deceased Imam is presented in the corpus as something that happened and as something the Imams ﵈ themselves taught about their own dead.

## Knowledge That Keeps Arriving

The reports on continuing knowledge are the corpus's strongest statements about the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams ﵈ after death. The reports call each Imam the wasi of the prophet before him, rendered in the translations variously as legatee, successor or executor and as trustee below, and they carry a scope distinction between the dead and the living trustee.

> [!info]- The Friday-night ascent, Imam al-Sadiq , al-Kafi, vol. 1, pp. 301-302
> (باب) * (في أن الأئمة ﵈ يزدادون في ليلة الجمعة) * 1 - حدثني أحمد بن إدريس القمي ومحمد بن يحيى ، عن الحسن بن علي الكوفي عن موسى بن سعدان ، عن عبد الله بن أيوب ، عن أبي يحيى الصنعاني ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : قال لي : يا أبا يحيى إن لنا في ليالي الجمعة لشأنا من الشأن ، قال قلت جعلت فداك وما ذاك الشأن قال : يؤذن لأرواح الأنبياء الموتى ﵈ وأرواح الأوصياء
>
> Chapter on the Imams increasing on Friday night.
>
> Ahmad ibn Idris al-Qummi and Muhammad ibn Yahya related to me from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abd Allah ibn Ayyub, from Abu Yahya al-San'ani, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, "He said to me, 'O Abu Yahya, on Friday nights we have an affair of great importance.'
>
> I said, 'May I be your ransom, and what is that affair?'
>
> He said, 'Permission is given to the souls of the deceased prophets and the souls of the legatees'

> [!info]- The Friday-night ascent, continued, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 302
> الموتى وروح الوصي الذي بين ظهرانيكم ، يعرج بها إلى السماء حتى توافي عرش ربها ، فتطوف به أسبوعا وتصلي عند كل قائمة من قوائم العرش ركعتين ، ثم ترد إلى الأبدان التي كانت فيها فتصبح الأنبياء والأوصياء قد ملؤا سرورا ويصبح الوصي الذي بين ظهرانيكم وقد زيد في علمه مثل جم الغفير .
>
> of the deceased, and the soul of the successor who is among you, to ascend to heaven until they reach the Throne of their Lord. They circumambulate it seven times and pray two units of prayer at each support of the Throne. Then they are returned to the bodies in which they had been. The prophets and successors awake filled with joy, and the successor who is among you awakes with an increase in his knowledge as abundant as a vast multitude."

The next report is broader.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq  to Mufaddal, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 302
> 2 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن أبي زاهر ، عن جعفر بن محمد الكوفي ، عن يوسف الابزاري ، عن المفضل قال : قال لي أبو عبد الله ﵇ ذات يوم وكان لا يكنيني قبل ذلك : يا أبا عبد الله قال : قلت : لبيك ، قال : إن لنا في كل ليلة جمعة سرورا قلت زادك الله وما ذاك ؟ قال : إذا كان ليلة الجمعة وافى رسول الله ﵌ العرش ووافى الأئمة ﵈ معه ووافينا معهم ، فلا ترد أرواحنا إلى أبداننا إلا بعلم مستفاد ، ولولا ذلك لأنفدنا .
>
> Muhammad ibn Yahya related from Ahmad ibn Abi Zahir, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Yusuf al-Abzari, from al-Mufaddal, who said, "One day Abu Abd Allah said to me, though he had not previously addressed me by a kunyah, 'O Abu Abd Allah.'
>
> I said, 'At your service.'
>
> He said, 'Every Friday night we have joy.'
>
> I said, 'May God increase you. What is that?'
>
> He said, 'When Friday night comes, the Messenger of God comes to the Throne, the Imams come with him, and we come with them. Our souls are returned to our bodies only with newly acquired knowledge. Were it not for that, what we have would run out.'"

Here the words are the first person plural of the living Imam speaking with all of them, our souls are not returned to our bodies except with newly acquired knowledge, and were it not so, what we have would run out. A third report, from al-Baqir to Zurara on the next page, says the same in the first person and makes the order of transmission explicit. The two reports together support the ascent, the worship, and the reception of knowledge, with the explicit increase wording resting on the living trustee's phrase.

> [!info]- Imam al-Baqir  to Zurara, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 303
> 3 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن ابن أبي نصر ، عن ثعلبة ، عن زرارة قال : سمعت أبا جعفر ﵇ يقول : لولا أنا نزداد لأنفدنا ، قال : قلت : تزدادون شيئا لا يعلمه رسول الله ﵌ ؟ قال : أما إنه إذا كان ذلك عرض على رسول الله ﵌ ثم على الأئمة ثم انتهى الامر إلينا .
>
> Muhammad ibn Yahya related from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Tha'laba, from Zurara, who said, "I heard Abu Ja'far say, 'Were we not to increase, we would run out.'
>
> I said, 'Do you increase in something that the Messenger of God does not know?'
>
> He said, 'Indeed, when that occurs, it is presented to the Messenger of God, then to the Imams, and then the matter reaches us.'"

The next report states the same order as a rule.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 303
> 4 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن محمد بن عيسى ، عن يونس بن عبد الرحمن ، عن بعض أصحابه ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : ليس يخرج شئ من عند الله ﷿ حتى يبدأ برسول الله ﵌ ثم بأمير المؤمنين ﵇ ثم بواحد بعد واحد ، لكيلا يكون آخرنا أعلم من أولنا .
>
> Ali ibn Ibrahim related from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from one of his companions, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, "Nothing comes forth from God until it begins with the Messenger of God, then the Commander of the Faithful, then one after another, so that the last of us may not be more knowledgeable than the first of us."

These are the corpus's strongest direct reports that the Prophet ﷺ and the earlier Imams ﵈ continue to receive information after their deaths, and the knowledge is described as received from Allah and passed in order, not as self-originating.

Basa'ir al-Darajat devotes a chapter to this acquired knowledge.

> [!info]- The chapter on acquired knowledge, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 152
> (6) حدثنا أحمد بن إسحاق عن الحسن بن عباس بن حريش عن أبي جعفر ﵇ قال قال أبو عبد الله ﵇ والله ان أرواحنا وارواح النبيين لتوافى العرش ليلة كل جمعة فما ترد في أبداننا الا بجم الغفير من العلم .
>
> Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us from al-Hasan ibn Abbas ibn Huraysh, from Abu Ja'far, who said, "Abu Abd Allah said, 'By God, our souls and the souls of the prophets come to the Throne on every Friday night. They are returned to our bodies only with a vast abundance of knowledge.'"

> [!info]- The chapter, continued, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 152
> (7) حدثنا محمد بن إسحاق بن سعد عن الحسن بن عباس بن حريش عن أبي جعفر ﵇ قال قال رسول الله ﵌ ان أرواحنا وارواح النبيين توافي العرش كل ليلة جمعة فتصبح الأوصياء وقد زيد في علمهم مثل جم الغفير من العلم .
>
> Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'd related to us from al-Hasan ibn Abbas ibn Huraysh, from Abu Ja'far, who said, "The Messenger of God said, 'Our souls and the souls of the prophets come to the Throne every Friday night, and the legatees awaken having been increased in their knowledge by an amount like a vast abundance of knowledge.'"

The chapter's reports speak of their souls not returning to their bodies except with a great abundance of knowledge, in the same frame as al-Kafi's, and both routes pass through al-Hasan ibn Abbas ibn Huraysh, so they are one textual witness.

## Their Bodies, Raised or Preserved

The reports on what happens to the body divide, and the corpus prints the division openly.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , al-Kafi, vol. 4, p. 567
> 1 - عدة من أصحابنا ، عن أحمد بن محمد ، عن علي بن الحكم ، عن زياد بن أبي الحلال ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : ما من نبي ولا وصي نبي يبقى في الأرض أكثر من ثلاثة أيام حتى ترفع روحه وعظمه ولحمه إلى السماء وإنما تؤتى مواضع آثارهم ويبلغونهم من بعيد السلام ويسمعونهم في مواضع آثارهم من قريب .
>
> A number of our companions related from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hilal, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, "No prophet or legatee of a prophet remains in the earth for more than three days before his soul, bones, and flesh are raised to heaven. Rather, the sites of their traces are visited, greetings are conveyed to them from afar, and they hear them nearby at the sites of their traces."

The clause that matters for the practice of visiting is the last one, greetings reach them from far away and they hear at the places of their traces from near. Al-Tusi transmits the same report with its own chain to the same teachers.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , al-Tusi, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, p. 106
> (186) 2 - محمد بن أحمد بن داود القمي عن أبيه عن محمد بن الحسن الصفار عن أحمد بن محمد عن علي بن الحكم عن زياد بن أبي الحلال عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : ما من نبي ولا وصي يبقى في الأرض بعد موته أكثر من ثلاثة أيام حتى ترفع روحه وعظمه ولحمه إلى السماء ، وإنما تؤتى مواضع آثارهم ويبلغهم السلام من بعيد ويسمعونه في موضع آثارهم من قريب .
>
> Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Qummi related from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hilal, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, "No prophet or legatee remains in the earth after his death for more than three days before his soul, bones, and flesh are raised to heaven. Rather, the sites of their traces are visited, greetings are conveyed to them from afar, and they hear it nearby at the sites of their traces."

On the same page he transmits a second report with a different interval.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq , the forty-day report, in al-Tusi, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, p. 106
> (185) 1 - الشيخ ﵀ قال : أخبرني الشريف الفاضل أبو عبد الله محمد بن محمد بن طاهر الموسوي عن أحمد بن محمد بن سعيد عن علي بن الحسن ابن فضال عن أخيه أحمد عن العلا بن يحيى أخي مغلس عن عمرو بن زياد عن عطية الابزاري قال : سمعت أبا عبد الله (﵇) يقول : لا تمكث جثة نبي ولا وصي نبي في الأرض أكثر من أربعين يوما .
>
> Al-Tusi said, "The noble and learned Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Tahir al-Musawi informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from his brother Ahmad, from al-Ala ibn Yahya, the brother of Mughallis, from Amr ibn Ziyad, from Atiyya al-Abzari, who said, 'I heard Abu Abd Allah say, "The body of no prophet or legatee of a prophet remains in the earth for more than forty days."'"

Three days in one report, forty in another, both printed by the same compiler with their chains. The page also carries the narrative of Ali's ﵇ burial.

> [!note]- The burial of Ali , in al-Tusi, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, pp. 106-107
> (187) 3 - محمد بن أحمد بن داود القمي قال : أخبرني محمد بن علي ابن الفضل قال : أخبرني علي بن الحسين بن يعقوب من بني خزيمة قراءة عليه قال : حدثني جعفر بن محمد بن يوسف الأزدي قال : حدثنا علي بن بزرج الخياط قال : حدثنا عمرو قال : جاءني سعد الإسكاف قال : يا بني تحمل الحديث ؟ فقلت : نعم فقال : حدثني أبو عبد الله (﵇) قال : انه لما أصيب أمير المؤمنين (﵇) قال للحسن والحسين صلوات الله عليهما : غسلاني وكفناني وحنطاني واحملاني على سريري واحملا مؤخره تكفيان مقدمه ، فإنكما تنتهيان إلى قبر محفور ولحد ملحود ولبن موضوع
>
> Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Qummi said, "Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Fadl informed me. He said, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ya'qub, of Banu Khuzayma, informed me by reading it to him. He said, "Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Azdi related to me. He said, 'Ali ibn Buzurj the tailor related to us. He said, "Amr related to us. He said, 'Sa'd al-Iskaf came to me and said, "O my son, do you carry hadith?" I said, "Yes." He said, "Abu Abd Allah related to me that when the Commander of the Faithful was struck, he said to al-Hasan and al-Husayn, 'Wash me, shroud me, perfume me with hanut, carry me upon my bier, and carry the rear of it; you two will suffice for its front. You will come to a dug grave, a prepared burial niche, and bricks set in place'"'"'"'"

> [!note]- The burial, continued, Tahdhib al-Ahkam, vol. 6, p. 107
> فألحداني وأشرجا اللبن علي وارفعا لبنة مما يلي رأسي فانظرا ما تسمعان ، فأخذا اللبنة من عند الرأس بعد ما أشرجا عليه اللبن فإذا ليس في القبر شئ وإذا هاتف يهتف : أمير المؤمنين (﵇) كان عبدا صالحا فالحقه الله بنبيه وكذلك يفعل بالأوصياء بعد الأنبياء ، حتى لو أن نبيا مات في المشرق ومات وصيه في المغرب لألحق الله الوصي بالنبي .
>
> Lay me in a niche grave, set the bricks over me with clay, and lift a brick from the side of my head and see what you hear." They took the brick from beside his head after setting the clay over him, and there was nothing in the grave. Then a caller called out, "The Commander of the Faithful was a righteous servant, so God joined him to His Prophet. Thus He does with the executors after the prophets. Even if a prophet died in the east and his executor died in the west, God would join the executor to the prophet."

On the other side stand reports and arguments for the body remaining. The Amali of al-Tusi transmits the account of the officer al-Mutawakkil sent to efface the grave.

> [!note]- Ibrahim al-Dizaj's account, in al-Tusi, al-Amali, p. 356, report 653
> 653 / 100 - أخبرنا ابن خشيش ، عن محمد بن عبد الله ، قال : حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الله بن محمد بن عمار الثقفي الكاتب ، قال . حدثنا علي بن محمد بن سليمان النوفلي ، عن أبي علي الحسين بن محمد بن مسلمة بن أبي عبيدة بن محمد بن عمار ابن ياسر ، قال : حدثني إبراهيم الديزج ، قال : بعثني المتوكل إلى كربلاء لتغيير قبر الحسين (﵇) ، وكتب معي إلى جعفر بن محمد بن عمار القاضي : أعلمك أني قد بعثت إبراهيم الديزج إلى كربلاء لنبش قبر الحسين ، فإذا قرأت كتابي فقف على الامر حتى تعرف فعل أو لم يفعل . قال الديزج : فعرفني جعفر بن محمد بن عمار ما كتب به إليه ، ففعلت ما أمرني به جعفر بن محمد بن عمار ثم أتيته ، فقال لي . ما صنعت ؟ فقلت : قد فعلت ما أمرت به ، فلم أر شيئا ولم أجد شيئا . فقال . لي : أفلا عمقته ؟ قلت : قد فعلت وما رأيت ، فكتب إلى السلطان : إن إبراهيم الديزج قد نبش فلم يجد شيئا وأمرته فمخره بالماء ، وكربه بالبقر . قال أبو علي العماري : فحدثني إبراهيم الديزج ، وسألته عن صورة الامر ، فقال لي . أتيت في خاصة غلماني فقط ، وإني نبشت فوجدت بارية جديدة وعليها بدن الحسين بن علي ووجدت منه رائحة المسك ، فتركت البارية على حالتها وبدن الحسين على البارية ، وأمرت بطرح التراب عليه ، وأطلقت عليه الماء ، وأمرت بالبقر لتمخره وتحرثه فلم تطأه البقر ، وكانت إذا جاءت إلى الموضع رجعت عنه ، فحلفت لغلماني بالله وبالايمان المغلظة لئن ذكر أحد هذا لأقتلنه .
>
> 653/100. Ibn Hashish informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Thaqafi the scribe, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Nufali, from Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Maslama, that Ibrahim al-Dizaj related to him, "Al-Mutawakkil sent me to Karbala to alter the grave of al-Husayn. He wrote with me to Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar, the judge, 'I inform you that I have sent Ibrahim al-Dizaj to Karbala to exhume the grave of al-Husayn. When you read my letter, attend to the matter until you know whether he has done it or not.'"
>
> Al-Dizaj said, "Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar told me what had been written to him. I did what he ordered me to do, then I came to him. He said to me, 'What have you done?' I said, 'I have done what you ordered me to do. I saw nothing and found nothing.' He said to me, 'Did you not dig deeper?' I said, 'I did, and I saw nothing.' So he wrote to the ruler that Ibrahim al-Dizaj had exhumed it and found nothing, and that he had ordered him to let water run over it and plow it with cattle.
>
> Abu Ali al-Amari said, "Ibrahim al-Dizaj related to me, and I asked him about how the matter had occurred. He said to me, 'I came with only my own slave boys. I exhumed it and found a new mat, with the body of al-Husayn ibn Ali upon it. I smelled musk from him. So I left the mat as it was and the body of al-Husayn upon the mat. I ordered earth to be thrown over it and released water over it. I ordered cattle to run over it and plow it, but the cattle would not tread upon it, and whenever they came to the spot, they turned back from it. I made my servants swear by God, with solemn oaths, that if any one of them mentioned this, I would kill him.'"

Al-Dizaj tells the caliph's judge that he found nothing and tells his servants the rest. Inside one report the public telling and the confidential one differ, and the corpus's body texts may diverge the same way. This report is one instance, not a rule.

Sayyid Jafar Murtada al-Amili surveys both groups of texts and the attempts to reconcile them.

> [!tip]- Sayyid Jafar Murtada al-Amili, Mukhtasar Mufid, vol. 6, p. 13
> فإن رفع الأجساد إلى السماء ، ليس بالأمر الذي يصح التشكيك فيه ، بعد تصريح القرآن ، وتواتر الحديث به . . فإن معراج نبينا الأعظم بجسده وروحه ، ثابت بلا ريب ، وقد أشارت إليه آيات القرآن الكريم (1) . . والأحاديث الشريفة المتواترة . . وهذا دليل على الوقوع فضلاً عن الإمكان . . كما أن الله تعالى قد أشار إلى رفع النبي إدريس ﵇ ، إلى السماء * (وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَاناً عَلِيّاً) * (2) . وقد صرحت الروايات بأن الله تعالى قد قبض روحه هناك (3) . . كما أن النبي عيسى ﵇ ، قد رفعه الله إليه ، كما صرحت به الآيات الكريمة . قال تعالى : * (إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ) * وقال : * (بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللهُ إِلَيْهِ) * (4) والروايات قد أكدت ذلك أيضاً (5) . .
>
> The raising of bodies to heaven is not a matter that can properly be doubted after the Quran has stated it explicitly and reports about it have been transmitted through recurrent transmission.
>
> The ascension of our greatest Prophet in body and spirit is established beyond doubt. The noble verses of the Quran have indicated it, as have the recurrent noble reports.
>
> This is evidence of its occurrence, quite apart from its possibility.
>
> God Most High has also indicated that He raised the Prophet Idris to heaven. "And We raised him to a high place." The reports have stated explicitly that God Most High took his soul there.
>
> Likewise, God raised the Prophet Jesus to Himself, as the noble verses state explicitly. He Most High said, "I will take you in full and raise you to Me," and He said, "Rather, God raised him to Himself." The reports have also confirmed this.

> [!tip]- The same survey, continued, Mukhtasar Mufid, vol. 6, p. 20
> وإذا كان الأمر كذلك ، فإن الحصول على هذا العظم لا يتناقض مع النصوص القائلة : إن أجساد الأنبياء لا تفنى ، فلعل الجسد باق ، وقد بقي معه ما دفن من أجزاء منفصلة عنه . . كالظفر ، والسن ، وما إلى ذلك . . بل إن الآيات القرآنية والأحاديث الشريفة قد دلت على أن المجرمين والطغاة كانوا يقتلون النبيين بغير حق ، وكانوا يقطعون أجسادهم بالمناشير . . فلعل هذا الجزء من ذلك الجسد الطاهر قد قطع ثم دفن . وهو لم يفن بعد . . حديث زيارة عظام آدم ويوسف : وأما بالنسبة لحديث المفضل بن عمر ، حول زيارة عظام النبي آدم ، وبدن النبي نوح ، وجسم الإمام علي ﵈ ، فنقول : أولاً : إن الحديث لا يصرح بموضع وجود تلك العظام ، وذلك البدن ، أو الجسد ، فلعلها رفعت في السماء ، لكن زيارتها في ذلك الموضع الذي كانت قد دفنت فيه توجب وصول السلام والزيارة إلى المزور عن قرب (1) ، لخصوصية في موضع الدفن . .
>
> If this is so, then obtaining this bone does not conflict with the texts stating that the bodies of the prophets do not decay. Perhaps the body remains, along with what was buried with it of parts separated from it, such as a nail, a tooth, and the like.
>
> Indeed, Quranic verses and noble reports indicate that criminals and tyrants used to kill the prophets unjustly and cut their bodies with saws. Perhaps this part of that pure body was cut off and then buried, and it has not yet decayed.
>
> The report concerning the visitation of the bones of Adam and Joseph.
>
> As for the report of al-Mufaddal ibn Umar concerning the visitation of the bones of the Prophet Adam, the body of the Prophet Noah, and the body of Imam Ali, we say the following.
>
> First, the report does not state explicitly where those bones, that body, or that corporeal form are located. Perhaps they were raised to heaven, but visiting them at the place where they had been buried causes the greeting and visitation to reach the one visited nearby, due to a particular quality of the place of burial.

His position is that the raising of the bodies is established, by the ascension of some prophets and by other texts, and that the reports of bodies remaining are then read as the deposited parts, the severed pieces, or the honour of the burial place. The next extract answers two reports his questioner had raised, a monk said to have kept a bone of a prophet, and al-Mufaddal's instruction to greet the bones of Adam, the body of Noah and the body of Ali. The reconciliation is his, and it is offered as an argument, not as a report. Qur'an 3:169 settles neither the location nor the condition of a martyr's buried body, and nothing in the practice of asking at a grave requires settling it. What the body texts do carry is that the one greeted is reachable wherever the body is, the three-day report itself says the greetings reach them.

## Seen Awake and in Dreams

Several reports narrate encounters with the dead while awake, and they are a different class of evidence from dreams. The clearest is in al-Kafi.

> [!info]- The chain, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 580
> 11 - محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى ، ومحمد بن أبي عبد الله ومحمد بن الحسن عن سهل بن زياد جميعا ، عن الحسن بن العباس بن الجريش (2) ، عن أبي جعفر الثاني ﵇ أن أمير المؤمنين ﵇ قال لابن عباس : إن ليلة القدر في كل سنة ، وإنه ينزل في تلك الليلة
>
> 11 - Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Muhammad ibn Abi Abd Allah and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, all from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Jarish (2), from Abu Ja'far the Second, that the Commander of the Faithful said to Ibn Abbas, "Laylat al-Qadr occurs in every year, and on that night there descends"

> [!info]- The chain, continued, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 581
> أمر السنة ولذلك الامر ولاة بعد رسول الله ﵌ ، فقال ابن عباس : من هم ؟ قال : أنا وأحد عشر من صلبي أئمة محدثون .
>
> The command of the Sunna, and that command has governors after the Messenger of God. Ibn Abbas said, "Who are they?" He said, "I and eleven from my loins, Imams who are spoken to."

> [!info]- The report of Ali  and Abu Bakr, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 581
> 13 - وبهذا الاسناد أن أمير المؤمنين ﵇ قال لأبي بكر يوما : " لا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون " وأشهد [أن] محمدا ﵌ رسول الله مات شهيدا والله ليأتينك ، فأيقن إذا جاءك فان الشيطان غير متخيل (1) به فأخذ علي بيد أبي بكر فأراه النبي ﵌ فقال له : يا أبا بكر آمن بعلي وبأحد عشر من ولده ، إنهم مثلي إلا النبوة وتب إلى الله مما في يدك ، فإنه لا حق لك فيه ، قال ثم ذهب فلم ير (2)
>
> 13. Through this chain of transmission, the Commander of the Faithful said to Abu Bakr one day, "Do not suppose that those who have been killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive, receiving provision from their Lord." And I bear witness that Muhammad, the Messenger of God, died a martyr. By God, he will surely come to you. So be certain when he comes to you, for Satan cannot assume his appearance.
>
> Then Ali took Abu Bakr by the hand and showed him the Prophet. He said to him, "O Abu Bakr, believe in Ali and in eleven of his descendants. They are like me, except for prophethood. Repent to God from what is in your hand, for you have no right to it." Then he departed and was not seen.

The report mentions no dream. Abu Bakr here is the first caliph after the Prophet's death, and the command to repent of what is in his hand concerns the leadership he holds. The chain is a single route through Sahl ibn Ziyad and al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Jarish, left ungraded here. The account describes no grave opening and no body rising, so it is no proof about the buried body.

Basa'ir al-Darajat gathers such reports under a chapter title of its own, that the Imams ﵈ visit the dead and the dead visit them.

> [!info]- Imam al-Rida , in al-Saffar, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 294
> (5) باب في أن الأئمة ﵈ يزورون الموتى وان الموتى يزورهم . (1) حدثنا معاوية بن حكيم عن الحسين بن علي الوشا عن أبي الحسن الرضا ﵇ قال قال لي بخراسان رأيت رسول الله ﵌ هيهنا والتزمته .
>
> (5) Chapter on the fact that the Imams visit the dead and that the dead visit them.
>
> (1) Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida, who said to me in Khurasan, "I saw the Messenger of God here and embraced him."

> [!note]- The encounter at the Quba mosque, Basa'ir al-Darajat, p. 294
> (2) حدثنا محمد بن عيسى عن ابن أبي عمير وعلي بن الحكم بن مسكين عن ابن عمارة عن أبي عبد الله وعثمان بن عيسى عن أبان بن تغلب عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ ان أمير المؤمنين ﵇ لقى أبا بكر فاحتج عليه ثم قال له اما ترضى برسول الله ﵌ بيني وبينك قال فكيف لي به فاخذ بيده واتى مسجد قبا فإذا رسول الله ﵌ فيه فقضى على أبى بكر فرجع أبو بكر مذعورا فلقي عمر فأخبره فقال مالك اما علمت سحر بني هاشم .
>
> (2) Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ali ibn al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ibn Ammarah, from Abu Abd Allah, and from Uthman ibn Isa, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abd Allah, that the Commander of the Faithful met Abu Bakr and argued his case against him. Then he said to him, "Are you not satisfied to have the Messenger of God judge between you and me?"
>
> He said, "How can I get to him?"
>
> So he took his hand and brought him to the Mosque of Quba. There was the Messenger of God in it, and he rendered judgment against Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr returned terrified and met Umar, informing him of it. Umar said, "What is wrong with you? Did you not know the sorcery of the Banu Hashim?"

In the Quba account the Prophet ﷺ renders judgment against Abu Bakr, and the report itself records Umar's dismissal, the sorcery of Banu Hashim. Umar is the second caliph. The book carries several versions of the Quba scene on the following pages (pp. 296-299), one of them explicitly beginning from an unnamed transmitter, and several versions of one encounter are not several independent confirmations of it.

Dreams are reported as dreams.

The dream saying of the Prophet ﷺ is quoted inside a dream narrative al-Tusi's Amali carries a few pages earlier, in which Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, a Kufan Quran-reader of the generation after the Imams, a different man from the first caliph, dreams of al-Husayn's shrine at Karbala, its courtyard closed for the visitation of Abraham and Muhammad with Gabriel and Michael, and wakes to find the dream pointing him to the grave (pp. 353-354).

> [!info]- The Prophet  on dreams, quoted in al-Tusi, al-Amali, p. 354
> فإن موضعا يأتيه إبراهيم ومحمد وجبرئيل وميكائيل (﵈) لحقيق بأن يرغب في إتيانه وزيارته ، فإن أبا حصين حدثني أن رسول الله (﵌) قال : من رآني في المنام فإياي رأى ، فإن الشيطان لا يتشبه بي .
>
> A place visited by Abraham, Muhammad, Gabriel, and Michael is surely worthy of being desired and visited. Abu Husayn told me that the Messenger of God said, "Whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me, for Satan cannot take my likeness."

The commander sent with al-Dizaj reports his deathbed account in the Amali as well.

> [!note]- The dream warning to the commander, in al-Tusi, al-Amali, pp. 356-357, report 654

A dream report narrates contact in a dream; each stands on its own chain. Both classes presuppose what the waking reports state, that the dead are not absent. What a waking encounter adds over a dream, and what the grave instructions add over both, is the visitor's own address, attributed to the Imams, for the standing supplication at the grave.

## The Same Act in the Sunni Canon

The reports above are Shia. The act they describe, addressing a deceased Imam by name and seeking Allah through him, is carried by the Sunni canon as well, in texts its own scholars graded, and the Sunni form addresses the Prophet ﷺ himself. The report has him teaching it to a blind man.

> [!info]- The Prophet's  instruction to the blind man, Sunan al-Tirmidhi, vol. 5, p. 569
> 3578 - حَدَّثَنَا مَحْمُودُ بْنُ غَيْلَانَ قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عُمَرَ قَالَ : حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ ، عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ ، عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ حُنَيْفٍ ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا ضَرِيرَ البَصَرِ أَتَى النَّبِيَّ ﷺ فَقَالَ : ادْعُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُعَافِيَنِي قَالَ : « إِنْ شِئْتَ دَعَوْتُ ، وَإِنْ شِئْتَ صَبَرْتَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكَ » . قَالَ : فَادْعُهْ ، قَالَ : فَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَتَوَضَّأَ فَيُحْسِنَ وُضُوءَهُ وَيَدْعُوَ بِهَذَا الدُّعَاءِ : « اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ وَأَتَوَجَّهُ إِلَيْكَ بِنَبِيِّكَ مُحَمَّدٍ نَبِيِّ الرَّحْمَةِ ، إِنِّي تَوَجَّهْتُ بِكَ إِلَى رَبِّي فِي حَاجَتِي هَذِهِ لِتُقْضَى لِيَ ، اللَّهُمَّ فَشَفِّعْهُ فِيَّ » : هَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ غَرِيبٌ لَا نَعْرِفُهُ إِلَّا مِنْ هَذَا الوَجْهِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَهُوَ الْخَطْمِي
>
> 3578. Mahmud ibn Ghaylan related to us. Uthman ibn Umar related to us. Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, from Uthman ibn Hunayf, that a blind man came to the Prophet and said, "Supplicate to Allah to grant me well-being."
>
> He said, "If you wish, I will supplicate, and if you wish, be patient, for that is better for you."
>
> He said, "Then supplicate to Him."
>

I have turned through you to my Lord concerning this need of mine, so that it may be fulfilled for me. O Allah, accept his intercession for me."

> This is a hadith that is hasan, sahih, gharib. We know it only through this route, from the hadith of Abu Ja'far, who is al-Khatmi.

The blind man is told to perform ablution and then make the supplication, whose turn is in the second person, I have turned through you to my Lord in this need of mine. Al-Tirmidhi's judgment follows the text, hasan sahih gharib, good, authentic and of a single route in his grading, known only through Abu Ja'far al-Khatmi. Al-Hakim transmits it through Abu Jafar al-Madani from Imarah ibn Khuzayma.

Al-Hakim's grading follows the text, sahih al-isnad, his formula for an authentic chain in a report the two canonical collectors, al-Bukhari and Muslim, did not include. His version adds the vocative, O Muhammad, and the two units of prayer before the supplication. The form is an address to the Prophet ﷺ by name inside a prayer whose giver and grantor is Allah, the same structure the Shia visitation texts use.

The story's continuation carries the practice past the Prophet's ﷺ death, and it is documented in the Sunni hadith literature with its carriers named.

In the story, Uthman ibn Hunayf, the Companion who had witnessed the Prophet's ﷺ instruction, teaches a petitioner at the caliph Uthman ibn 'Affan's court the same supplication, with the Prophet ﷺ addressed by name after his death, and the need is met the same day. The Sunni canon also affirms, in its own texts, that the dead hear.

The reports carry the blessings, salah, reaching him wherever the sender is, and the one who sends them upon him at his grave is heard by him. The Companions' question, how the blessings could reach him after his body had decayed, is answered in Ibn Kathir's version of the same report.

> [!info]- The Prophet's  answer on his body, in Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim, vol. 6, p. 418

>

On it Adam was created, on it he died, on it will be the blast, and on it will be the thunderclap. So send abundant blessings upon me on it, for your blessings are presented to me.'"
>

>
> He said, "Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets."
>

The oldest form of seeking through the Prophet ﷺ is also carried there.

> [!note]- Adam asks by the right of Muhammad, in Ibn Asakir, Tarikh Madinat Dimashq, vol. 7, p. 386
> أخبرني رجل من أهل الكوفة من عباد الناس من الأنصار قال حدثني عبد الرحمن بن عبد ربه المازني من أهل البصرة عن شيخ من أهل المدينة من أصحاب عبد الله بن مسعود قال لما أصاب ادم الذنب نودي أن أخرج من جواري فخرج يمشي بين شجر الجنة فبدت عورته فجعل ينادي العفو العفو فإذا شجرة قد أخذت برأسه فظن أنها أمرت به فنادى بحق محمد ألا عفوت عني فخلي عنه ثم قيل له أتعرف محمدا قال نعم قيل وكيف قال لما نفخت في يا رب الروح رفعت رأسي إلى العرش فإذا فيه مكتوب محمد رسول الله (﵌) فعلمت أنك لم تخلق خلق أكرم عليك منه
>
> A man from the people of Kufah, one of the devout worshippers among the Ansar, informed me. He said, "'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Mazini, from the people of Basrah, related to me from an old man from the people of Madinah, who was among the companions of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud.
>
> When Adam committed the sin, he was called, 'Leave My vicinity.' So he went out, walking among the trees of Paradise, and his private parts became exposed. He began to call out, 'Pardon, pardon.' Then a tree caught hold of his head. He thought it had been commanded concerning him, so he called out, 'By the right of Muhammad, will You not pardon me?' So he was released.
>
> Then he was asked, 'Do you know Muhammad?'
>
> He said, 'Yes.'
>
> It was said, 'How?'
>
> He said, 'When, my Lord, You breathed the spirit into me, I raised my head to the Throne and found written upon it, "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." I knew that You had not created any creature more honored before You than he.'"

The report's chain, as printed, runs through two unnamed transmitters, a man of Kufa and a shaykh of Medina of the generation of Ibn Mas'ud's companions; it carries what the tradition itself transmits about the first supplication made through the Prophet ﷺ, before his creation in time as the reports frame it.

## The Hearing Objection

The strongest objection of the practice's opponents runs as follows. The Qur'an says to the Prophet ﷺ that he does not make the dead hear (Qur'an 27:80), and that he cannot make those in the graves hear (Qur'an 35:22). The dead do not hear, therefore no request addressed to them can be received, and addressing them is an innovation that led Noah's people into shirk, the worship of others beside Allah. Ibn Taymiyya states the practical ruling.

> [!tip]- Ibn Taymiyya, Majmu al-Fatawa, vol. 1, p. 171
> فَإِذَا كَانَ هَذَا مُحَرَّماً وَهُوَ سَبَبٌ لِسَخَطِ الرَّبِّ وَلَعْنَتِهِ فَكَيْفَ بِمَنْ يَقْصِدُ دُعَاءَ الْمَيِّتِ وَالدُّعَاءَ عِنْدَهُ وَبِهِ وَاعْتَقَدَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَسْبَابِ إجَابَةِ الدَّعَوَاتِ وَنَيْلِ الطَّلَبَاتِ وَقَضَاءِ الْحَاجَاتِ ؟ وَهَذَا كَانَ أَوَّلَ أَسْبَابِ الشِّرْكِ فِي قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعِبَادَةِ الْأَوْثَانِ فِي النَّاسِ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ : كَانَ بَيْنَ آدَمَ وَنُوحٍ عَشَرَةُ قُرُونٍ كُلُّهُمْ عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ ثُمَّ ظَهَرَ الشِّرْكُ بِسَبَبِ تَعْظِيمِ قُبُورِ صَالِحِيهِمْ .
>
> If this is forbidden, and it is a cause of the Lord's wrath and curse, then what of one who deliberately invokes the dead, supplicates at their graves and through them, and believes that this is among the means by which supplications are answered, requests are obtained, and needs are fulfilled?
>
> This was among the first causes of shirk among the people of Noah and of the worship of idols among people. Ibn 'Abbas said, "There were ten generations between Adam and Noah, all of them upon Islam. Then shirk appeared because of their veneration of the graves of their righteous people."

The danger his argument names, that grave-veneration opened the way to shirk, is real. The texts in evidence instruct the visitor to ask the dead Imam to pray to Allah, the act the Sunni canon carries in Tirmidhi's graded text and in the story of Uthman ibn Hunayf, and they do not instruct worship. The separate question, whether an address in this form already counts in its outward form as worship under the verses revealed about the idolaters of Mecca, is not settled here. On hearing itself, the Qur'an commentary (tafsir) of the objectors' own school limits what the proof text denies, and al-Shinqiti reads the parallel verse, 35:22, the same way (Adwa al-Bayan, vol. 6, p. 125).

> [!quote]- Qur'an 27:80
> إِنَّكَ لَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَلَا تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوْا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
>
> *innaka la tusmi'u l-mawta wa-la tusmi'u l-summa l-du'a'a idha wallaw mudbirin*
>
> Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating.

> [!tip]- Al-Shinqiti on the verse, Adwa al-Bayan, vol. 6, p. 122
> اعلم أن التحقيق الذي دلّت عليه القرائن القرءانيّة واستقراء القرءان ، أن معنى قوله : * ( إِنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتَى ) * ، لا يصح فيه من أقوال العلماء ، إلا تفسيران :
>
> Know that the sound conclusion indicated by Qur'anic contextual evidence and by surveying the Qur'an is that only two interpretations of the scholars are valid regarding the meaning of His saying, “Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear.”

> [!tip]- His first reading, continued, Adwa al-Bayan, vol. 6, p. 122
> الأول : أن المعنى : * ( إِنَّكَ لاَ تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتَى ) * ، أي : لا تسمع الكفار الذين أمات اللَّه قلوبهم ، وكتب عليهم الشقاء في سابق علمه إسماع هدى وانتفاع ؛ لأن اللَّه كتب عليهم الشقاء ، فختم على قلوبهم ، وعلى سمعهم ، وجعل على قلوبهم الأكنة ، وفي آذانهم الوقر
>
> The first is that the meaning of “Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear” is that you cannot make the disbelievers, whose hearts God has caused to die and upon whom He decreed wretchedness in His prior knowledge, hear in a way that brings guidance and benefit. For God decreed wretchedness for them, so He sealed their hearts and their hearing, and placed coverings over their hearts and heaviness in their ears.

> [!tip]- The second reading, and its ascription to Ibn Taymiyya, Adwa al-Bayan, vol. 6, p. 126
> فهكذا الموتى الذين ضرب بهم المثل لا يجب أن ينفى عنهم جميع أنواع السماع ، كما لم ينف ذلك عن الكفار ، بل قد انتفى عنهم السماع المعتاد الذين ينتفعون به ، وأمّا سماع آخر فلا ، وهذا التفسير الثاني جزم به واقتصر عليه أبو العباس ابن تيمية
>
> Thus, the dead who were used in the comparison need not be denied every kind of hearing, just as that was not denied of the disbelievers. Rather, they have been denied the ordinary hearing by which they benefit. As for another kind of hearing, it has not been denied. Abu al-'Abbas Ibn Taymiyya stated this second interpretation decisively and confined himself to it.

Al-Shinqiti states that no reading of the verse is sound except two. On the first, the dead of the verse are the disbelievers whose hearts Allah has killed, and the negated hearing is hearing that brings guidance and benefit. On the second, the negated hearing is the customary hearing from which the hearer benefits, and Ibn Taymiyya himself confined himself to this second reading. Neither reading denies that the dead can hear at all. On the second the objection survives only as the claim that the dead lack beneficial hearing, and the canon's own reports of the buried hearing sandals and of the Prophet ﷺ hearing blessings at his grave are that school's answer. Abu Dawud's footsteps report and the blessings reports in Fath al-Bari are not contradictions to be explained away. They are what the canon itself affirms.

On the chain of the post-death story, Ibn Taymiyya's objection is quoted in his own words.

> [!tip]- Ibn Taymiyya on the story's chain, Majmu al-Fatawa, vol. 1, p. 274
> قُلْت : وَقَدْ رَوَاهُ النَّسَائِي فِي كِتَابِ ( عَمَلُ الْيَوْمِ وَاللَّيْلَةِ ) مِنْ هَذِهِ الطَّرِيقِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ مُعَاذِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أُمَامَةَ سَهْلِ بْنِ حَنِيفٍ عَنْ عَمِّهِ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ حَنِيفٍ . وَرَوَاهُ أَيْضاً مِنْ حَدِيثِ شُعْبَةَ وَحَمَّادِ بْنِ سَلَمَةَ كِلَاهُمَا عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ خُزَيْمَة وَلَمْ يَرْوِهِ أَحَدٌ مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ - لَا التِّرْمِذِيُّ وَلَا النَّسَائِي وَلَا ابْنُ مَاجَه - مِنْ تِلْكَ الطَّرِيقِ الْغَرِيبَةِ الَّتِي فِيهَا الزِّيَادَةُ : طَرِيقُ شَبِيبِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ رَوْحِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ .
>
> I say that al-Nasa'i related it in the book Deeds of Day and Night through this route, from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Hisham, from his father, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu Umamah Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his uncle Uthman ibn Hunayf.
>
> He also related it from the hadith of Shu'bah and Hammad ibn Salamah, both from Abu Ja'far, from 'Umarah ibn Khuzaymah. None of these, neither al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, nor Ibn Majah, related through that uncommon route which contains the addition, the route of Shabib ibn Sa'id from Ruh ibn al-Qasim.

None of the three collectors, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, related the supplication through the single route that carries the addition, the post-death story, the route of Shabib ibn Sa'id from Ruh ibn al-Qasim, while al-Zabidi's documentation, naming al-Bayhaqi's Dalail al-Nubuwwa and the other carriers above, is the Sunni hadith literature's own record that the story circulates in its books. The dispute over this chain is a dispute inside the Sunni canon about one relay, not a finding that the practice lacks texts, and the gradings cited apply to the supplication itself.

## What the Evidence Supports

The evidence supports the claim the clearest instruction makes. Al-Husayn ﵇, in the reports, hears the visitor who stands at his grave, knows him, prays to Allah for him, and can be asked to pray for his need. The Prophet ﷺ and the Imams ﵈, in the reports, are alive with their Lord, aware of the deeds of the living, and receiving knowledge that arrives from Allah. The reports do not give the dead independent power. The effects they seek are sought from Allah, by the prayer of the one addressed. The Sunni canon carries the same structure in texts its scholars graded. That removes the assumption that the practice was invented by the Shia against the rest of the tradition.

The chains keep their limits, the isnad-less formula, the shared al-Asamm relay, the ungraded Ibn al-Jarish route, and the contested continuation relay, all printed above. None of this weakens the reports as witnesses of what the two traditions teach. All of it matters if the argument is pressed from attribution to authentication, a step this survey does not take.

What remains unsettled is the body, and the corpus itself is the reason, its reports divide and its own surveyors argue. The practice of asking rests on the hearing and the intercession, and the three-day report itself carries the greetings reaching them from far away and heard from near.

blocks.text: Alive with Their Lord - the Prophet and the Imams after Death in the Hadith Corpus

No verse of the Qur'an tells a believer to ask a deceased Imam for help, and the nearest texts, among them the instruction to come to the Messenger while he is alive and seek Allah's forgiveness with his prayer for them (Qur'an 4:64), concern the living. The question is whether the book and the reports together support the practice, and what exactly they support when they do. The Imams below are the twelve descendants of the Prophet through Ali and Fatima, and the corpus is the hadith literature of the school beside the Sunni books the later sections quote. Three passages supply principles. The martyrs are alive with their Lord, receiving provision (Qur'an 3:169). Allah, His Messenger and the believers see the deeds that people do (Qur'an 9:105). A servant can be granted an extraordinary capacity, and using it remains Allah's favour (Qur'an 27:40). None of these verses names a grave, a visitor, or a request.

The reports supply that step. A person with a need is told to stand at the head of al-Husayn ﵇ and address him with the words, I testify that you witness my standing and hear my words, and that you are alive with your Lord receiving provision, so ask your Lord and my Lord to fulfil my needs. Other reports describe the dead Imam seeing his visitors by name and praying for the one who weeps at his grave, the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams receiving further knowledge after death, and in several accounts the dead appearing to the living while awake.
Each report below is quoted as a contiguous extract from its source, with the chain where the source prints one.

Evidence What it carries Chain as printed The grave instruction Address al-Husayn ﵇, you hear me, you are alive, ask Allah for me Ibn Fahd introduces it with "it is reported from al-Sadiq ﵇", without an isnad (chain) A chained instruction for both graves Visit Ali ﵇ and al-Husayn ﵇ and turn there with your needs Ibn Uqda, through Hammad ibn Yala, from Hassan ibn Mihran The visitation texts The visitor addresses al-Husayn ﵇ and seeks Allah through him Liturgies in Kamil al-Ziyarat and Tahdhib al-Ahkam Al-Husayn ﵇ sees his visitors He knows them by name, seeks forgiveness for the one who weeps, and asks his father to seek it Two routes in Kamil al-Ziyarat, both through al-Asamm Knowledge after death The souls of dead prophets and trustees ascend and return with new knowledge al-Kafi, several routes, and Basa'ir al-Darajat The bodies Raised after three days, or forty days, or preserved; the corpus carries all three al-Kafi 4:567, Tahdhib 6:106-107, al-Amali, surveyed in Mukhtasar Mufid Appearances awake and in dreams The Prophet ﷺ shown to Abu Bakr; dreams distinguished from waking encounters al-Kafi 1:580-581 through Ibn al-Jarish; Basa'ir; al-Amali The Sunni canon The Prophet's ﷺ own supplication (du'a) with its turn through him; al-Hakim's text adds the vocative, and a Companion teaches it after his death Tirmidhi hasan sahih gharib; al-Hakim sahih al-isnad; the story in al-Zabidi's takhrij (documentation) The hearing objection That the dead do not hear, from Qur'an 27:80 and 35:22 Stated by Ibn Taymiyya, Majmu al-Fatawa 1:171; answered by al-Shinqiti's two readings and Abu Dawud's report
